title: `transaction()` context manager is silently broken
description: `_execute_transaction` is an `async def` with `yield session` (making it an async generator), passed to `execute_with_retry` which calls `await operation()`. Awaiting an async generator call returns the generator object; the body (including `yield session`) never executes. Every caller of `repo.transaction()` receives no session and silently does nothing.
recommendation: Rewrite `_execute_transaction` as a plain `async def` returning a result, or use `asynccontextmanager` correctly by restructuring so the retry loop wraps the async context manager. Alternatively, refactor `transaction()` to use `db_manager.get_session()` directly.
acceptance_test_hint: `async with repo.transaction() as session: await session.execute(text("SELECT 1"))` executes without error and returns a valid result.

title: Three column names in migration 001 do not match ORM schema
description: Lines 97 and 131 reference `confidence_score` (actual column is `confidence` in `Recommendation`); line 177 references `is_tradeable` (actual column is `is_tradable` in `Stock`). All three `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` calls will fail with `ERROR: column does not exist` on a clean database, leaving the schema partially applied.
recommendation: Fix column names: `confidence_score` → `confidence`; `is_tradeable` → `is_tradable`. Re-test by running `alembic upgrade head` against a fresh database.
acceptance_test_hint: `alembic upgrade 001_critical_indexes` completes without error; `\d recommendations` shows the new indexes.

title: Inline `INDEX(...)` clause inside `CREATE TABLE` is invalid PostgreSQL syntax
description: `api_usage_log` table definition (lines 134-146) uses `INDEX (provider, request_timestamp)` and `INDEX (request_timestamp) WHERE success = FALSE` as column constraints inside the `CREATE TABLE` body. PostgreSQL does not support this syntax — MySQL does. The entire table creation will fail with a parse error.
recommendation: Move the index definitions to separate `CREATE INDEX` statements after the `CREATE TABLE` block.
acceptance_test_hint: `psql -f infrastructure/database/optimizations.sql` produces no error; `\d api_usage_log` shows both indexes present.

title: Migration creates index on non-existent `watchlists.stock_id` column
description: `op.create_index('idx_watchlists_stock_id', 'watchlists', ['stock_id'])` — the `watchlists` table (as defined in `unified_models.py` lines 801-820) has no `stock_id` column. `stock_id` lives in `watchlist_items`. This migration will fail with `ERROR: column "stock_id" does not exist` on any database matching the ORM schema.
recommendation: Remove `op.create_index('idx_watchlists_stock_id', 'watchlists', ...)` from upgrade and the corresponding `drop_index` from downgrade. If an index on watchlist-to-stock lookups is needed, add it to `watchlist_items`.
acceptance_test_hint: `alembic upgrade adba55bf7b52` completes without error; `\d watchlists` confirms no phantom column.

title: `add_performance_indexes.sql` creates index on non-existent `watchlists.stock_id`
description: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_watchlists_user_id_stock_id ON watchlists(user_id, stock_id)` — same phantom column as F-07-005. Will silently fail on `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` if the column is absent, leaving an incomplete index set.
recommendation: Remove line 18. Create a `watchlist_items(watchlist_id, stock_id)` covering index instead.
acceptance_test_hint: `psql -f backend/migrations/add_performance_indexes.sql` completes without error.

title: Exchange/Sector/Industry→Stock relationships use `lazy="selectin"` globally
description: `Exchange.stocks`, `Sector.stocks`, `Sector.industries`, and `Industry.stocks` are all defined with `lazy="selectin"`. Any query fetching a single `Exchange`, `Sector`, or `Industry` row will immediately issue additional SELECT queries loading every associated `Stock` record — potentially thousands per lookup. This pattern was chosen to prevent `MissingGreenlet` in async context, but applies even when stock data is not needed.
recommendation: Change these reverse collection relationships to `lazy="select"` (lazy load on attribute access) or `lazy="raise"` (raise if accidentally accessed) and rely on `selectinload()` in queries that genuinely need the stock list. Alternatively use `lazy="noload"` and explicitly opt-in.
acceptance_test_hint: `GET /api/v1/stocks/?sector=Technology` does not emit more than 2 SQL queries (verified via SQLAlchemy echo or `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`).

title: `get_by_sector()` queries non-existent field `sector`
description: `FilterCriteria(field='sector', operator='eq', value=sector)` — `Stock` has no attribute `sector`. The field is `sector_id` (FK to sectors table). `_apply_filter` will raise `AttributeError: Stock has no field 'sector'` at runtime.
recommendation: Fix: change `field='sector'` to perform a JOIN on the `Sector` table, filtering by `Sector.name`. Use `select(Stock).join(Sector).where(Sector.name == sector)` pattern consistent with other join-based repository methods.
acceptance_test_hint: `await stock_repo.get_by_sector("Technology")` returns a list of stocks without raising.

title: `Position` ORM model missing `version` column added by migration
description: `add_row_locking_versions.sql` adds `version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` to the `positions` table (line 17). The `Position` class in `unified_models.py` has no `version` column (confirmed: lines 664–706 show no such column). Reads from `positions` after migration runs will have a DB column not reflected in the ORM, causing SQLAlchemy to silently ignore it. Optimistic locking for positions is thus non-functional despite being documented.
recommendation: Add `version = Column(Integer, default=1, nullable=False, server_default='1')` to the `Position` model. Create an Alembic migration to align the ORM with the existing SQL migration.
acceptance_test_hint: `position.version` returns an integer; `update_with_lock` on a `Position` increments version correctly.

title: ML training code misplaced in `backend/models/`
description: `backend/models/ml_models.py` (1,191 lines) contains PyTorch/sklearn ensemble training classes (`StockPredictionEnsemble`, `LSTMModel`, etc.) — not ORM schemas. It is not imported by any repository or API module (confirmed by scope-11 dead-code methodology applied here). Its presence pollutes the models package with ML runtime dependencies (torch, xgboost, prophet, optuna) that inflate import times for the entire ORM layer.
recommendation: Move to `backend/ml/` (already exists per scope-03). Update any remaining importers.
acceptance_test_hint: `from backend.models import unified_models` does not trigger torch/xgboost imports; `import time` of the models package drops measurably.

title: Mutable `dict`/`list` literals used as SQLAlchemy `Column` defaults
description: `Column(JSON, default={})` at lines 102, 967, 1128 and `Column(JSON, default=["email"])` at line 842. SQLAlchemy evaluates the `default` expression once at class definition time. All rows created without an explicit value share the same dict/list object — mutation of one row's JSON field can corrupt another in-memory until flushed.
recommendation: Replace with `default=dict` (callable) or `default=list` respectively. For dicts with initial values use a lambda: `default=lambda: {"email_daily_summary": True, ...}`.
acceptance_test_hint: `u1 = User(); u2 = User(); u1.preferences is not u2.preferences` evaluates `True`.

title: `price_history_optimized` table created by migration 006 is never referenced
description: Migration 006 creates `price_history_optimized` (a new optimized table) but neither `unified_models.py` nor any repository references this table. All production queries continue against `price_history`. The table is pure schema bloat.
recommendation: Either complete the migration by replacing `price_history` with `price_history_optimized` (add ORM model and update repositories), or drop the creation of `price_history_optimized` from migration 006 and replace with in-place alterations.
acceptance_test_hint: `SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE tablename = 'price_history_optimized'` returns 0 rows (or returns 1 and is referenced by an ORM model).

title: `UserSession` missing index on `expires_at` column
description: `UserSession.__table_args__` (lines 167-170) defines indexes on `session_token` and `(user_id, is_active)` but not on `expires_at`. Session expiry cleanup queries (`WHERE expires_at < NOW()`) and any auth middleware checking validity (`WHERE session_token = ? AND expires_at > NOW()`) will do full table scans as the sessions table grows.
recommendation: Add `Index('idx_session_expires_at', 'expires_at')` to `UserSession.__table_args__` and create a corresponding Alembic migration.
acceptance_test_hint: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM user_sessions WHERE expires_at < NOW() LIMIT 100` shows Index Scan, not Seq Scan.

title: `update()` unconditionally strips `None` values, preventing intentional NULL updates
description: `update_data = {k: v for k, v in update_data.items() if v is not None}` at lines 349 and 427 removes all `None` values before the UPDATE. Callers can never set a nullable column to NULL via the standard `update()` method (e.g., clearing `User.locked_until`, `Stock.ipo_date`).
recommendation: Use a sentinel value pattern: introduce a `UNSET = object()` sentinel and filter on `v is not UNSET` instead of `v is not None`, allowing callers to explicitly pass `None` for intentional NULL.
acceptance_test_hint: `await repo.update(id, {"locked_until": None})` results in `locked_until IS NULL` in the database row.

title: Two shim modules duplicate the same re-export of `unified_models`
description: `database.py` and `tables.py` both re-export nearly identical sets of symbols from `unified_models`. `tables.py` adds 8 enum classes not in `unified_models` (ModelTypeEnum, ModelStageEnum, etc.) but these enums have no DB-backed table. Having two shim modules for the same canonical source confuses callers and creates unnecessary import surface area.
recommendation: Merge `tables.py` enum additions into a single `backend/models/enums.py` and deprecate `tables.py`. Update `database.py` to document it is a backward-compat shim only, and add a deprecation warning on import.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "from backend.models.tables" backend/` and `grep -rn "from backend.models.database" backend/` return only legacy callers; all new code imports from `unified_models`.

title: Migration 002 `try/except` silently swallows TimescaleDB failures with no warning
description: The partitioning migration wraps every `op.execute(...)` TimescaleDB call in bare `except Exception: pass`. If TimescaleDB is not installed, the entire partitioning and compression setup silently does nothing — including the critical hypertable conversion. There is no log message, no status column, and no validation at end of migration.
recommendation: At minimum, log a warning when the TimescaleDB path is skipped: `logger.warning("TimescaleDB not available; falling back to manual partitioning")`. Add a post-migration validation query to verify the chosen path succeeded.
acceptance_test_hint: Migration 002 log output clearly indicates whether TimescaleDB or manual partitioning was applied.

title: `synchronous_commit = off` trades durability for throughput without documentation
description: `synchronous_commit = off` means PostgreSQL acknowledges commits before WAL records are flushed to disk. Up to ~200ms of committed transactions can be lost on a power failure. For an investment platform storing transaction records and portfolio positions, this is an unacceptable durability trade-off with no inline justification or per-table override strategy.
recommendation: Document the explicit risk decision inline. For tables storing financial transactions (`transactions`, `orders`, `positions`) consider `synchronous_commit = on` at the session level (SET LOCAL synchronous_commit = on) within those write paths.
acceptance_test_hint: `SHOW synchronous_commit` on a session writing to `transactions` returns `on` (or the risk decision is explicitly documented and signed off).

title: Two DB utility files with zero non-test importers (cross-scope confirm)
description: Scope-11 audit (F-11-003) identified `db_timescale_init.py` and `deadlock_handler.py` as dead code with no non-test importers. Confirmed via `grep -rn "db_timescale_init\
recommendation: deadlock_handler" backend/ --include="*.py"
acceptance_test_hint: grep -v test` returning only self-references within those files. These are out of this scope's path globs but have direct impact on DB persistence layer design. | Delegate deletion decision to scope-11. Cross-referencing here for completeness. | `grep -rn "from backend.utils.(db_timescale_init | deadlock_handler)" backend/` → 0 hits

title: Hardcoded KDF salt + low PBKDF2 iters
description: Fixed salt `b"investment_analysis_salt"` with 100k iters defeats salt purpose; weakens master-key derivation; allows offline brute force
recommendation: Generate per-installation salt; bump to ≥600k iters or migrate to Argon2id; re-encrypt all stored secrets
acceptance_test_hint: Two instances with same MASTER_SECRET_KEY produce different Fernet keys; PBKDF2 timing >250ms

title: In-memory RateLimiter per-process
description: `self.clock` dict per-instance, per-worker; effective limit = configured × N workers
recommendation: Delete this class; route through advanced_rate_limiter (Redis-backed)
acceptance_test_hint: grep returns 0 imports

title: DB-backed multi-role assignment loses state
description: `assign_role` adds to in-memory set but persists via `User.role` (single column); 2nd role overwrites 1st on restart
recommendation: Either declare single-role-only or add user_roles join table
acceptance_test_hint: Test: assign two roles, restart, assert both present

title: Baseline polluted with 1500+ lockfile false positives
description: NPM integrity hashes from .claude/v3/ dilute signal
recommendation: Add lockfile path-exclude; rebuild baseline
acceptance_test_hint: <100 entries after cleanup

title: stopwords list contains the keywords meant to flag secrets
description: gitleaks downgrades any line with `password`, `bearer`, `token`, `api`, `key`, `secret`, `auth` — the opposite of intent
recommendation: Remove stopwords block or scope to true noise (`example`, `template`)
acceptance_test_hint: gitleaks finds known seeded credential

title: File upload allowlist permits .txt without magic-byte verification
description: Polyglot HTML+JS renamed .txt could bypass content-type sniff
recommendation: Always set Content-Disposition: attachment; never serve user files from same-origin
acceptance_test_hint: Test attachment disposition

description: Test pass rate diverges from production security posture
recommendation: Compose; provide TestingSecurityProfile; integration test with TESTING=false
acceptance_test_hint: full-stack-enabled test runs all middlewares

title: CODEMAPS lists 7 of 20 security modules
description: secrets_manager, audit_logging, injection_prevention, input_validation, advanced_rate_limiter, csrf_protection undocumented
recommendation: Regenerate codemap from filesystem
acceptance_test_hint: wc -l matches documented count

title: Empty __init__ in single-file subpackage
description: No re-exports; imports use full path; package layer adds no value
recommendation: Consolidate oauth2.py into backend/security/ OR add re-exports
acceptance_test_hint: grep -r 'from backend.auth import' returns 0

title: No tests for FiduciaryDutyChecker
description: SEC-critical compliance code untested per CODEMAPS test matrix
recommendation: Add backend/tests/compliance/test_sec_fiduciary.py with ≥5 test cases
acceptance_test_hint: pytest -k fiduciary ≥5 tests

title: Custom registry isolation hides all SLA, health, and alerting Prometheus metrics
description: `metrics_collector.py` creates a private `CollectorRegistry` (line 35) and `generate_latest(registry)` (line 658) serves only that registry at `/metrics`. All metrics in `health_checks.py`, `alerting_system.py`, `application_monitoring.py`, `financial_monitoring.py`, and `database_performance.py` register to the **default** Prometheus registry (no `registry=` argument passed). `generate_latest()` (no args) for the default registry is never called. Result: Prometheus scrapes `/metrics` and gets only system/API/cost metrics — zero health-check, zero SLA compliance, zero alert metrics are exported.
recommendation: Unify all monitoring modules onto one registry. Either (a) pass the custom `registry` object to every `Gauge/Counter/Histogram` instantiation in all monitoring submodules, or (b) remove the custom registry from `metrics_collector.py` and call `generate_latest()` (no args) so all modules contribute to the default registry. Option (b) requires checking for name collisions first (see F-10-002).
acceptance_test_hint: `curl http://localhost:8000/metrics` returns text containing `health_check_status` and `sla_compliance_percent`; Prometheus target shows no missing series for health alerts.

title: `MimeText`/`MimeMultipart` import typo — email alerts silently fail at module load
description: Line 25: `from email.mime.text import MimeText` and line 26: `from email.mime.multipart import MimeMultipart`. The stdlib classes are `MIMEText` and `MIMEMultipart` (all-caps MIME prefix). Python raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'MimeText'` on any import of this module. Lines 409 and 420 also reference `MimeMultipart()` and `MimeText(html_body, 'html')` using the incorrect names. Since `__init__.py` imports `alertmanager_webhook` (not `real_time_alerts`) the module may not fail at startup unless imported elsewhere, but all email alert delivery paths are broken.
recommendation: Change line 25 to `from email.mime.text import MIMEText`, line 26 to `from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart`, line 409 to `msg = MIMEMultipart()`, and line 420 to `msg.attach(MIMEText(html_body, 'html'))`.
acceptance_test_hint: `python -c "from backend.monitoring.real_time_alerts import AlertSeverity"` exits 0 with no ImportError; integration test sends a test alert email.

title: `get_quality_summary` imported from `data_quality_metrics` does not exist
description: `metrics_collector.py:486` executes `from backend.monitoring.data_quality_metrics import get_quality_summary`. `data_quality_metrics.py` exports only `DataQualityMetricsCollector` (class, line 176) and `check_data_quality_with_metrics` (async function, line 543); no `get_quality_summary` function exists. The `ImportError` is caught by the surrounding `except Exception` at line 516, so `collect_data_quality_metrics()` silently fails every 10-second collection cycle. Gauges `data_quality_score`, `data_missing_percent`, and `data_staleness` are never populated.
recommendation: Implement `get_quality_summary()` in `data_quality_metrics.py` as a synchronous wrapper around `DataQualityMetricsCollector.get_summary()`, or change the call site to use `await check_data_quality_with_metrics(...)`.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "def get_quality_summary" backend/monitoring/data_quality_metrics.py` returns a hit; `data_quality_score` gauge has non-zero values in Prometheus after one collection cycle.

title: Counter internal `_value._value` mutated directly — breaks Prometheus atomicity guarantees
description: Lines 296-297: `network_bytes_sent.labels(interface='total')._value._value = net_io.bytes_sent` and `network_bytes_received.labels(interface='total')._value._value = net_io.bytes_recv`. This accesses the private internal attribute of a `Counter` object, bypassing the thread-safe increment API. Counters must be monotonically increasing; direct assignment can make the counter go backwards (e.g., if `net_io_counters()` resets after a reboot), violating Prometheus data model. Also breaks with any Prometheus client library version upgrade.
recommendation: Counters of cumulative OS bytes should use a `Gauge` not a `Counter` (or use `REGISTRY` provided by node-exporter instead). Replace with `Gauge('network_bytes_sent_total', ...)` and call `.set(net_io.bytes_sent)`. Or remove and rely on node-exporter's `node_network_transmit_bytes_total`.
acceptance_test_hint: `network_bytes_sent_total` (renamed to Gauge) has monotonically non-decreasing values over multiple scrapes; no `_value._value` references remain in metrics_collector.

title: Error budget recording rule uses 6-hour window — cannot represent 30-day monthly budget
description: `slo:error_budget_remaining:ratio` (line 187) is derived from `slo:api_availability:ratio_rate6h`, a 6-hour rolling average. The comment at line 4 states the error budget is "~43 min/month downtime." Using a 6-hour window means: (a) the budget resets every 6 hours, so sustained low-level degradation never exhausts it; (b) a 1-hour outage looks catastrophic on the 6h window but "recovers" as soon as the window rolls past. `SLOErrorBudgetLow` and `SLOErrorBudgetExhausted` will not fire under gradual availability erosion.
recommendation: Use Prometheus recording rules over a 30-day window: `sum_over_time(slo:api_availability:ratio_rate5m[30d])` or integrate with a purpose-built error budget tool (Sloth, Pyrra). At minimum replace the 6h reference with a 30d `avg_over_time`.
acceptance_test_hint: `slo:error_budget_remaining:ratio` decreases monotonically over the course of a simulated 30-day load test with 0.1% error injection; `SLOErrorBudgetLow` fires before the end of the month.

title: `gc_collections` Counter incremented with current GC count on every cycle — monotonicity violated
description: Lines 310-311: `for i, count in enumerate(gc.get_count()): gc_collections.labels(generation=str(i)).inc(count)`. `gc.get_count()` returns the current number of collections since the **last** `gc.collect()` call, not since program start. On each 10-second collection loop, this increments the counter by a small number (typically 0-10), not the true cumulative GC count. The Prometheus `rate()` over this counter will be meaningful on average, but `gc.get_count()` does not reset between calls, so values are not deltas — they represent a rolling window internal to CPython's GC. The correct approach is to use `gc.get_stats()` which returns per-generation collection counts since program start.
recommendation: Replace `gc.get_count()` with `gc.get_stats()` which returns a list of dicts with `'collected'` key representing cumulative total. Use `gc_collections.labels(generation=str(i))._value.set(stats['collected'])` with a Gauge, or track the delta manually.
acceptance_test_hint: `rate(gc_collections_total[5m])` in Prometheus returns a smooth non-spiky value during a GC-heavy workload; no counter resets visible in metrics.

title: Duplicate and divergent prometheus.yml in `config/monitoring/` — older stale copy
description: `config/monitoring/prometheus.yml` (57 lines) and `infrastructure/monitoring/prometheus.yml` (86 lines) are both present and differ significantly: different `external_labels`, missing `rule_files` section in the config copy, missing Nginx/Celery/Airflow scrape jobs, different job names (`backend` vs `investment-api`), different `metrics_path` for the backend (`/metrics` vs `/api/metrics`). The `config/monitoring/` copy appears to be an earlier draft never removed. Two authoritative Prometheus configs cause confusion about which is deployed.
recommendation: Delete `config/monitoring/prometheus.yml`. The `infrastructure/monitoring/prometheus.yml` is the canonical config (has SLO rule references, complete scrape targets). Verify `docker-compose.yml` mounts `infrastructure/monitoring/prometheus.yml` as the active config.
acceptance_test_hint: `find . -name "prometheus.yml" -not -path "*/infrastructure/monitoring/*"` returns no hits; docker-compose volume mount references `infrastructure/monitoring/prometheus.yml`.

title: `on_event("startup"/"shutdown")` deprecated FastAPI lifecycle hooks
description: `metrics_collector.py:675` uses `@app.on_event("startup")` and `@app.on_event("shutdown")`. These decorators were deprecated in FastAPI 0.93 (released 2023-02) and removed in FastAPI 0.110+. The recommended pattern is `lifespan` context manager. If the application runs FastAPI >= 0.110, metrics collection never starts and never stops cleanly.
recommendation: Replace with a `lifespan` async context manager: `from contextlib import asynccontextmanager; @asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app): await metrics_collector.start_collection(); yield; await metrics_collector.stop_collection()` and pass to `FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)`.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "on_event" backend/monitoring/metrics_collector.py` returns no hits; metrics collection starts on app startup (confirmed via log line "Started metrics collection").

title: Duplicate `HealthStatus` enum defined in `health_checks.py` and `health_system.py`
description: `health_checks.py:28` and `health_system.py:24` both define `class HealthStatus(Enum)` with identical values (`HEALTHY`, `DEGRADED`, `UNHEALTHY`, `CRITICAL`). Because they are separate enum classes, `HealthStatus.HEALTHY is health_system.HealthStatus.HEALTHY` is `False`. Any code that imports from one module and compares with a value from the other will fail equality checks silently. `__init__.py` uses `health_checks.setup_health_monitoring` while `health_system` is also imported independently.
recommendation: Delete `health_system.HealthStatus` and import it from `health_checks` (or move to a shared `backend/monitoring/types.py`). Ensure all references in `health_system.py` use the imported type.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "class HealthStatus" backend/monitoring/` returns exactly 1 hit; `isinstance(health_system.ServiceHealth(...).status, health_checks.HealthStatus)` is `True`.

title: `sla_tracker` uses `get_redis()` which is subject to the fail-open vulnerability (F-08-008)
description: `sla_tracker.py:16` imports `from backend.utils.cache import get_redis`; line 224 sets `self.redis = await get_redis()`. The auth scope audit (F-08-008) found that `redis_resilience.py` fails open — when Redis is unavailable, it returns a no-op client instead of raising. In `sla_tracker.py`, if Redis is in fail-open mode, SLA measurements silently succeed (`redis.set()` returns `True`) but are written to a no-op sink. SLA compliance records appear normal while actually empty.
recommendation: Add a Redis connectivity check before recording SLA measurements: verify `self.redis` is not the fail-open stub before `redis.set()`. At minimum log a warning when Redis is in fail-open mode. Cross-reference scope 08 fix for the underlying fail-open issue.
acceptance_test_hint: `sla_tracker` raises `SLAStorageUnavailableError` (or logs a warning) when Redis is in fail-open mode; SLA measurements are not silently discarded.

title: Dev Prometheus config scrapes backend at `/api/metrics` but endpoint is `/metrics`
description: `prometheus.yml:30` sets `metrics_path: /api/metrics` for the `investment-api` job. `metrics_collector.py:669` registers `@app.get("/metrics")`. The correct scrape path is `/metrics`, not `/api/metrics`. In development, Prometheus will receive 404 responses for every scrape of the backend, producing `up{job="investment-api"} == 0` and triggering the `ServiceDown` alert continuously.
recommendation: Change `prometheus.yml:30` from `metrics_path: /api/metrics` to `metrics_path: /metrics`. (The prod config already has the correct path at `prometheus.prod.yml:43`.)
acceptance_test_hint: `prometheus.yml` scrape config for `investment-api` has `metrics_path: /metrics`; Prometheus target page shows `investment-api` as UP.

title: `sla_compliance` Gauge label set differs between served custom registry and default registry instance
description: `metrics_collector.py:200` defines `sla_compliance = Gauge('sla_compliance_percent', ..., ['service'], registry=registry)` (1 label). `health_checks.py:66` defines `sla_compliance = Gauge('sla_compliance_percent', ..., ['service', 'sla_type', 'time_window'])` (3 labels) in the default (unserved) registry. The two definitions use different label sets for the same metric name. If F-10-001 is fixed by unifying to one registry, this will cause a Prometheus duplicate registration error at startup.
recommendation: Consolidate to a single definition with the richer label set `['service', 'sla_type', 'time_window']` in one shared location. Remove the duplicate from whichever module is not the canonical owner.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "sla_compliance_percent" backend/monitoring/` returns exactly 1 definition; Prometheus startup logs show no `duplicate metrics collector registration` error.

title: Test suite queries `/api/health/metrics` but the metrics endpoint is `/metrics`
description: `test_monitoring_api.py:86,112,142,168` all call `client.get("/api/health/metrics")`. The actual endpoint registered in `metrics_collector.py:669` is `/metrics`. These tests would pass only if a separate health router also exposes a `/api/health/metrics` path — unconfirmed. If no such route exists, every test in `TestMetricsEndpoint` passes a 404 response without asserting the correct status code (tests would need to be checked for assertion strength).
recommendation: Update all test assertions to call `/metrics` instead of `/api/health/metrics`, and add an explicit `assert response.status_code == 200` at the start of each test.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/test_monitoring_api.py::TestMetricsEndpoint` exits 0 with all assertions against `response.status_code == 200`.

title: Elasticsearch setup code executes on every instantiation despite being permanently disabled
description: `log_analysis.py:585-601` `_setup_elasticsearch()` is called in `__init__`. Even though Elasticsearch is optional and the import is guarded at lines 26-30, the setup method still checks `AsyncElasticsearch is not None` and reads env vars on every `LogAnalysisSystem()` construction. This is dead execution — the env var `ELASTICSEARCH_URL` is never set (Elasticsearch was removed to save $15-20/month per PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZATION.md). 20+ lines of dead setup code run pointlessly.
recommendation: Remove `_setup_elasticsearch()` and its call from `__init__`, or guard the entire method behind an explicit `ENABLE_ELASTICSEARCH=true` feature flag that defaults off.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "_setup_elasticsearch\ | elasticsearch_client" backend/monitoring/log_analysis.py` returns 0 hits (after cleanup).
